evidence.requirements: Every requirement is met as written. The three tastings have the exact data in server/tastings.ts:9-13. The start page shows title, date/time, 'EUR n per guest' and '<n> seats left' (TastingsPage.tsx:21-31, format.ts:16; start.jpg). Each card has a 'Book <title>' link (TastingsPage.tsx:35-37). The form has the fields Name, Email, Guests (1–8) and a 'Book' button (BookingPage.tsx:75-113). Validation errors appear next to the field they concern (form.jpg: 'Enter a valid email address' under Email). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:30-41; confirmation.jpg: EUR 64 for 2×32). /staff has a Password field, a Sign in button and uses STAFF_PASSWORD (StaffPage.tsx:156-169, index.ts:10). Bookings are grouped by tasting with name, email, guests, reference and a Cancel button (staff.jpg). Cancelling frees seats (app.ts:133-138). Fully booked state: TastingsPage.tsx:25-28 and BookingPage.tsx:64-67. Mobile layout: .playwright-mcp/home-mobile.png. Stack: React, Express 5, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, Tailwind. Bookings in memory, PORT defaults to 3000.
evidence.correctness: The seat check runs synchronously before push (app.ts:78-85). Node handles requests on one thread, so concurrent requests cannot overbook. Fully booked and 'Only n seats left' cases return 409 with a guests field error (app.ts:79-81), and the client maps that to the field and revalidates (BookingPage.tsx:44-49). Zod enforces int, 1–8, trimmed name with a 100-character max, and a valid email (shared/api.ts:5-21). The same schema runs on client and server. Cancel removes the booking, so seatsTaken recomputes (app.ts:136). Unknown tasting gives 404, malformed JSON gives a JSON 400 (app.ts:144-147). References are generated with crypto randomInt and checked for collisions (app.ts:58-64). Dates are formatted at fixed UTC noon so the day doesn't shift across time zones (format.ts:4). I found no logic bugs.
evidence.security: The password check hashes both sides and uses timingSafeEqual (staff.ts:5-12). Sign-in is refused when no password is set (staff.ts:7). Session tokens are 32 random bytes in a server-side Map with a TTL (staff.ts:14-38). The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict, with Secure set behind a trusted proxy (app.ts:65). Sign-out deletes the session server-side (app.ts:113-116). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited (app.ts:95-102), and README:21 warns about TRUST_PROXY spoofing. The public booking lookup leaves out name and email (app.ts:48-57, test at api.test.ts:54-62). React escapes all output, and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. There are no secrets in code. Minor gap: no security headers such as helmet or CSP.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: server/app.ts is a testable factory, index.ts handles static files and the listener, shared/api.ts holds the schema and types for both sides, and there is one file per page plus small Field and format helpers. Names are clear. Error handling covers API errors, 401, 404 and root form errors (BookingPage.tsx:43-53, StaffPage.tsx:43-54). It uses react-router loaders and revalidation idiomatically. There is no needless abstraction, and the size fits the task.
evidence.tests: tests/api.test.ts has 25 supertest cases covering the main backend rules. These include the seat listing, the confirmation payload and total, the seat limit and singular message, fully booked, per-field validation including the boundaries 0, 9, 2.5, a string '2' and 101 characters, and unknown tasting. On the staff side they cover auth, the no-password case, cookie flags, grouped listing, cancel freeing seats, cancel without a session, sign-out, expiry and the lockout. The client has no tests at all: no component or e2e tests check the labels, the 'Book <title>' text, errors shown next to fields, or the confirmation heading.
evidence.ux_design: start.jpg shows a coherent winery look: burgundy serif headings, a parchment background, cards with clear prices and seats, and prominent book buttons. form.jpg shows a clear inline error with a highlighted field and a seats-left hint. confirmation.jpg has a distinct green success panel with a bold monospace reference. staff.jpg is tidy, with seat summaries per tasting. home-mobile.png shows a usable phone layout and a 'Fully booked' pill. Weaknesses: the design is fairly generic, with no imagery or brand touches. Staff Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation and no success feedback. The bordered error input in form.jpg reads as burgundy focus outline rather than red.
evidence.accessibility: There is lang=en (index.html:2). Fields use label/htmlFor, aria-invalid and aria-describedby linking the error and hint (Field.tsx, BookingPage.tsx:81-107). There is semantic header/nav/main/footer, sections labelled by their headings, and table th scope=col with an sr-only Actions header (StaffPage.tsx:97-104). Buttons have focus-visible outlines and a min-h-11 target size. Contrast of the theme colours looks adequate. Gaps: field errors are not in a live region; on client validation react-hook-form focuses the first invalid field, but server-returned errors set through setError are neither focused nor announced. The repeated 'Cancel' buttons have no booking context for screen readers. The fully booked badge uses muted text on a beige background.
evidence.simplicity: There are 9 runtime dependencies (package.json:12-22), each with a clear job: Express, cookie-parser, express-rate-limit, React, react-router, react-hook-form with resolvers, and zod. Tailwind and Vite are dev-only. The code totals about 700 lines with no over-engineering, and one validation schema is shared between client and server.
evidence.maintainability: README covers run steps, environment variables (including TRUST_PROXY), behaviour such as in-memory storage, session length and lockout, and the scripts. There is a lockfile, strict TypeScript and a typecheck script. Missing: no CI pipeline, no engines field or .nvmrc pinning Node 22, and caret version ranges. There are no specs, ADRs or other decision records, even though the brief asked for a spec-driven process. There is no staff manual, no changelog or release approach, and no client regression tests. Agent artefacts in .playwright-mcp are left in the folder, though gitignored.

strengths: The backend is correct and well tested: seat limits, fully booked and validation boundaries, cancelling frees seats, and the shared zod schema enforces the rules on both client and server (app.ts:71-87, shared/api.ts, 25 API tests).

Staff security is strong: hashed timingSafeEqual comparison, server-side random session tokens with TTL and sign-out, HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookies, sign-in rate limiting, and sign-in refused when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset.

The UI is clean and coherent for a winery and works on a phone, with clear error, success and fully booked states (start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg, home-mobile.png). It uses established libraries idiomatically.
issues: Maintainability gaps: no CI pipeline, no Node version pinning (engines/.nvmrc), no specs/ADRs or staff guide, and no release or versioning approach.
No client or e2e tests: the visible labels, button texts, errors shown next to fields and the confirmation page are not covered by any regression test.

Staff Cancel deletes a booking instantly with no confirmation or success message, and the repeated 'Cancel' buttons have no booking context for screen readers. Server-side field errors are not announced or focused.
review.verdict: This is a correct, secure and tidy implementation that meets every brief requirement, backed by thorough API tests and a pleasant, phone-friendly winery design. It falls short of excellent mainly on project maintainability (no CI, no version pinning, no decision docs), no UI tests, and small staff UX and accessibility gaps around cancelling.
